Subject: Question on charges during pilot — unusually high per-day cost

Hey Rohan / Tessa,

Quick one from our finance team as we started the pilot yesterday: our daily invoice looks much higher than forecasted. We expected the baseline pilot SKU (~15k tokens/day) but the line item labeled "service-unit aggregation" seems to be billing many small calls individually and hitting a per-utterance floor frequently.

Can you explain: 1) whether short helper calls (e.g., 40–120 token classifier calls that happen between user interactions) are billed against the same session bucket or separately; 2) how the per-utterance minimum gets applied vs. session amortization when prefix reuse happens across requests; and 3) whether there are any immediate packaging adjustments you can offer while we debug our client-side batching?

Attached is the sample invoice from today. Appreciate a breakdown — cc'ing our billing mailbox.

Thanks,

From: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Question on charges during pilot — unusually high per-day cost

Hi Jordan — thanks for the invoice and the clear notes. Short answer up front: the behavior you saw is expected with your current call pattern, but we have two clear remediation paths (client-side batching + a temporary packaging concession). Below is a concise breakdown, then proposed next steps.

Billing model explanation (how units were counted today):
- Service-unit aggregation: we bill on a per-token basis but with a per-request minimum "quantum" applied to small independent requests. That minimum exists to avoid microbilling overhead for sub-40-token requests.
- Session amortization: when requests are part of the same conversation context (same session id and contiguous KV cache), we amortize prefix tokens across calls. However, calls that are created as separate sessions or that expire the KV cache (idle > 5 minutes in your config) will not get amortized and will incur the full minimum on small requests.
- Prefix reuse / KV cache: if you reuse the exact same prefix and the request hits the warm KV cache on the same serving instance, you'll see much lower per-call effective cost; if it falls back (cold) or is routed to a different instance, the first call pays for prefix tokens.

Why your invoice looked high: based on the sample, your webhook executes many short classifier calls (40–120 tokens) as separate HTTP calls with different session ids. Each of those hit the min-quantum, which multiplied across thousands of calls.

Proposed immediate options:
1) Short-term packaging concession (pilot): Kimberly (cc) can propose a temporary microfloor credit to reduce the per-utterance minimum impact for the first 90 days while you optimize client batching.
2) Client changes: batch helper calls into a single request or keep a session open (reuse session id / maintain heartbeat) to enable prefix amortization and KV cache reuse.
3) Longer-term: switch the pilot to a per-session billing SKU (commit-oriented) that charges for an amortized block rather than per-call quantums. That requires minor contract adjustments.

I attached a short mapping spreadsheet that shows how your sample day maps to unit charges with and without amortization.

If you want, we can run a 48-hour re-instrumentation with tracing flags enabled to prove gains from batching (no charge for that proof run).

Action requested: let us know which remediation you'd prefer (1 = temporary concession, 2 = run with hints for 48-hour test, 3 = switch to per-session pilot SKU). I'll loop in contracts if we move to #3.

Thanks —

Subject: Re: Service-unit aggregation & per-utterance floor — ACME pilot packaging

Jordan — looping in billing. We approve a temporary concession for pilot customers experiencing microfloor overage due to helper-call patterns. Proposed concession details:

- 15% credit applied to per-utterance quantum charges for the first 90 days of the pilot (applies only to calls < 250 tokens that are flagged as helper-classifier calls).
- We will also convert your current pilot SKU to a metric-called "amortized-session-credits" for the duration if you opt in; this converts small per-call quantums into aggregated session credits on the monthly invoice (no contract change required for a 90-day pilot concession).

Constraints:
- The credit cannot be applied retroactively prior to the concession start date (we can offer a one-time goodwill credit if needed, to be reviewed by finance).
- We need a short instrumented log sample to ensure classifiers are consistently flagged as helper calls (Rohan's mapping sheet will help).

I'll prepare a short amendment note for your procurement team if you accept the 90-day concession and per-session view.

Kimberly Park
Director, Pricing & Packages | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

1) How will the helper-classifier calls be identified on the invoice? Will there be a distinct line item or tag we can reconcile against our usage exports?
2) For the amortized-session-credits option, what telemetry do you need from our side to prove calls are part of the same session (session id, KV warm flag, or timestamp proximity)?

If both are straightforward we'll take the 90-day concession and the amortized-session-credits view. Also please set expectations for when the first adjusted invoice will appear — we need it for our month-end close.

Jordan

Jordan — great, thanks for the quick response and for confirming. Final notes and next steps: 

1) Invoice visibility / tagging: we'll surface a new invoice line item "Helper-call quantum credits (pilot concession)" and tag helper-classifier calls in the usage export with a helper_call boolean. That will let your finance team do a clean reconciliation. Expect the tagging to show in the next daily export (we'll enable it on our side at 00:00 UTC next day).

2) Telemetry for amortization: the minimal telemetry we need is session_id and a kv_cache_warm boolean per request; timestamp proximity (gap < 5min) is used as a fallback for older SDKs. We'll share a short instrumented snippet to paste into your client.

3) Timeline & credits: Kimberly will kick off the concession (15% credit) effective 2029-04-21 00:00 UTC for 90 days. Please confirm if you want a one-time goodwill credit for the period 2029-04-18 to 2029-04-20 while we switch tagging on; we can route that request to finance for expedited review.

4) Proof run: we'll run the 48-hour no-charge batching proof as proposed. Rohan and Tessa will coordinate. Expected completion 2029-04-23.

5) Action items (mutual action plan):
- ACME: enable session_id telemetry + kv_cache_warm flag (I will send the snippet).
- Redwood: enable helper_call tagging & apply concession starting 2029-04-21; run a 48-hour proof run starting when ACME toggles telemetry.
- Both: review adjusted export and sample invoice on 2029-04-24; if savings consistent, we'll convert pilot to amortized-session-credits view.
